samples.summary: Share-link `viewer` write authorization is still off by default (shadow mode allow-all); the branch's own docs state a viewer link is write-capable on a stock deployment
samples.evidence: `handleAuth` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:149-164) computes a deny (`hasAccess` → `link.role === 'editor'` for a `rw` verb, line 262) and then returns `{allowed:true}` with HTTP 200 whenever `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'` (line 116). Nothing in the repo sets that variable: I grepped every yml/yaml/env/json/sh and found no deployment config, and there is no code that registers the webhook methods on the Yorkie project either (no `authWebhookMethods` anywhere). Attack: hold any viewer-role share link → `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` (auth.controller.ts:82-90, public, no session needed) mints a Yorkie token wrapping the share token → attach with a bare `@yorkie-js/sdk` client using `VITE_YORKIE_PUBLIC_KEY`, which ships in every visitor's bundle (shared-document.tsx:957) → PushPull writes to `note-<id>` are allowed because the only gate that would refuse them is bypassed at line 149. This change is the one that expands the share surface (toolbar + `shareTokenImageUploader` on the notes route) while the enforced path stays disabled, and the new docs (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md Risks, packages/backend/README.md, packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:57-67) explicitly acknowledge it. Pre-existing and deliberate as a staged rollout — but the effective default posture is an authorization bypass for anonymous viewer links, and the only mitigation added here is a boot-time log line.

samples.summary: Security documentation names the wrong (session-guarded) endpoint as the anonymous Yorkie-token mint, understating/mis-locating the vector
samples.evidence: The new doc comment says a share-link viewer's token "mints a Yorkie token at `GET /auth/yorkie-token`". That route is `@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)` and mints from `req.user.id` (auth.controller.ts:68-73) — an anonymous visitor cannot use it. The anonymous mint is `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` (auth.controller.ts:82-90). The same wrong endpoint is repeated in packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:61, packages/backend/README.md, docs/design/notes/notes.md and docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md. A reader auditing the vector will look at a guarded route and may conclude the gap is closed.

samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore`'s own doc comment contradicts itself about whether it is an access-control boundary
samples.evidence: Lines 57-67 state "It is **not** an access-control boundary, and the earlier claim here that it was ... was wrong"; line 71 then justifies the trap set with "because this is an access-control boundary, the ways around a bare `get` have to be covered too". A future reader deciding whether a new write path may skip the wrapper gets opposite answers from the same comment — the exact confusion the rest of the change was written to remove.

samples.summary: Share token (an edit-granting bearer credential) is sent in a URL query string on the upload the notes share route now uses
samples.evidence: `SharedNotesLayout` (shared-notes-layout.tsx:74) wires `shareTokenImageUploader(token)`, which calls `postShareTokenImage` → `POST /api/v1/shared/images?token=<share token>` (api/images.ts:51-62), and the backend reads it from `@Query('token')` (image-share-upload.controller.ts:95). Credentials in query strings land in reverse-proxy/CDN access logs and browser history. The repo already argues against exactly this for the same credential: `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` uses a body "so the (access-granting) token stays out of request URLs and access logs" (auth.controller.ts:76-80). Pre-existing for the docs share surface; this change extends the exposure to the notes share route.

samples.summary: Client-side role check fails open: anything that is not exactly "viewer" gets the editable surface and the share-token uploader
samples.evidence: `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer";` and `ResolvedShareLink.role` is typed `role: string` (packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:8,17), so any unrecognized role value (a future `commenter`, a typo, a role added server-side) yields `readOnly === false` → full formatting group, writable store (notes-view.tsx:152 keeps the raw `YorkieNoteStore`) and `shareTokenImageUploader(token)` (line 74). The backend does the inverse, fail-closed check (`link.role === 'editor'`, yorkie-auth.controller.ts:262; image-share-upload.controller.ts:135), so the client is the one side that widens on an unknown role. Today's roles are validated to `viewer|editor` at creation (share-link.service.ts:79), which is what keeps this latent rather than live. `role !== "editor"` would fail closed.

samples.summary: Unsanitized external `attr.key` interpolated into the shadow-mode log line (log forging)
samples.evidence: `target` is built from `body.attributes[].key`/`verb` (lines 156-158) and interpolated into a single-line `logger.warn` (line 160) before any validation — the deny path that logs includes `unknown document key`, i.e. keys `parseYorkieDocKey` rejected, so the value is arbitrary caller-supplied text. A key containing CR/LF (or a fake `reason=`/`token=` fragment) forges additional log records, which matters because these very lines are now the documented mitigation for shadow mode. Exploitability depends on Yorkie's own document-key validation and requires a request that passes `YorkieSignatureGuard`'s HMAC, so I could not confirm a reachable newline; escaping/whitelisting the key before logging would remove the doubt.

samples.summary: No test covers the frontend half of the read-only store guard (`notes-view.tsx`'s `readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(raw) : raw`), in the one package with no type checking
samples.evidence: The new guard is asserted at two of three layers: `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.test.ts` (the proxy) and `packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts` (the engine's own wrap). The frontend mount's wrap at notes-view.tsx:152 has no test — there is no `notes-view.test.tsx` (only notes-toolbar.test.tsx, yorkie-note-store.test.ts, notes-thumbnail.test.ts, notes-undo-integration.test.ts under packages/frontend/src/app/notes), and the new `shared-notes-layout.test.tsx` mocks `@/app/notes/notes-view` out entirely (lines 90-108), so nothing exercises the real component. packages/frontend runs no `tsc`, so silently dropping the wrap (e.g. reverting `storeRef` to `YorkieNoteStore`) would not be caught by any lane. Impact is limited to defence-in-depth, since the raw store is only handed to the guarded `initialize()` today.

samples.summary: An editor share token now also grants workspace-wide image object creation from the notes share route
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader(token)` posts to `ApiV1ShareImageUploadController`, which derives the prefix from `link.document.workspaceId` (image-share-upload.controller.ts:129-143), so a token scoped to one document can add objects anywhere in that workspace's image prefix, rate-limited to 30/min with no cumulative quota (comment at lines 62-75). Deliberate and documented for the docs share surface; this change makes it reachable from notes share links too, widening the storage-abuse surface for a leaked editor link.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate in every checked particular. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:115-116 defaults enforcement off (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'`), and lines 149-164 convert any computed deny into HTTP 200 `{allowed:true, reason:'shadow'}`. Line 262 (`return needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true;`, with needWrite set for verb `rw` at line 226) is the only server-side refusal of a share-link viewer write, and it is exactly what the shadow branch discards. The vector is reachable anonymously: auth.controller.ts:82-90 exposes `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` with no JwtAuthGuard (contrast the guarded `GET yorkie-token` at :68-69) and mints a Yorkie token wrapping any share token, deferring role validation to the webhook; share-link.service.ts:11,86 makes `viewer` the default role any member may mint; and shared-document.tsx:703,957 ships the Yorkie project apiKey in the visitor bundle, so an attacker can attach with a bare SDK client instead of the app's read-only mounts. No guard elsewhere closes this: grepping every occurrence of the variable shows it set to `true` only in specs (yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts:55, revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:292), docker-compose.yaml has no AUTH_WEBHOOK key, and self-hosting.md:185 documents the default as allow-everything. The controller's own comment at :86-99 and logPosture at :127-140 concede that client read-only mounts bound only this app. This is a missing authorization gate on the enforced path — in-lane and critical; its pre-existing/deliberate staged-rollout nature is decided separately and does not refute realness.

finding.summary: The viewer read-only guarantee this change builds on has no server-side enforcement in the default configuration — the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode, so every gate added here is client-side only
finding.evidence: `this.enforce = configService.get('YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE') === 'true'` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:101) defaults to false, and lines 111-119 then return ALLOW for a computed deny. `hasAccess()` would otherwise be the only thing refusing `link.role === 'viewer'` a write (line 217). Attack: a holder of a viewer-role share link calls `fetchYorkieShareToken(token)` (the frontend already does this at shared-document.tsx:959 and hands the result to the SDK), attaches with any Yorkie client outside the browser UI, and pushes arbitrary text ops to the note — no client-side `changeFilter`, `EditorState.readOnly` or `runHistory` guard is in the path. The diff's own comments (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:435-437, docs/design/notes/notes.md) acknowledge this, which makes it a known rollout state rather than a regression — but this change materially widens the surface that depends on it (a viewer is now given a live editor pane and the full `NoteEditorAPI` via the mounted toolbar), so it is worth restating that the boundary is unenforced by default. Mitigation is deployment-level (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`), not code.

verdict.reason: The described code exists (only the line numbers are shifted). yorkie-auth.controller.ts:115-116 defaults `enforce` to false when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE is unset, and 149-164 converts a computed deny into HTTP 200 with {allowed:true, reason:'shadow'}. Line 262 (needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true) is the only server-side refusal of a share-link viewer write, so in the default configuration it never takes effect. The vector is reachable: POST /auth/yorkie-token/share is public (auth/auth.controller.ts:82) and mints a Yorkie token from a viewer share token (frontend/src/api/auth.ts:187-193, consumed at shared-document.tsx:705,959), letting a viewer attach with any Yorkie client and push writes. No compensating server-side guard exists -- the other YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE consumers only gate the template public tier -- and the repo's own comments (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-99, logPosture 132-139) affirm the client read-only mounts bound only this app and are not an access-control boundary. This is missing/weakened access control, squarely in the Security lane; being a documented, deploy-time-mitigated rollout posture does not refute it, and I must not discount it for being pre-existing.
